cases.title: Rushed buyer shows time pressure in the answer

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I am leaving for a meeting in a minute.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Where does the delivery process get difficult?

cases.manual_review: Does attention/disclosure reflect being rushed, without a fixed word limit or a polished full workflow diagnosis?

cases.title: Buyer can give a short, vague answer

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Do those occasional order checks actually bother your team?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Not sure it is a big thing.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: What is your impression, without getting into the details?

cases.manual_review: Can uncertainty remain tentative and brief, without escalating pain or supplying a business case?

cases.title: Buyer does not have an operational metric

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I do not track handling time; it is not part of my role.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: How many minutes does each case lose?

cases.manual_review: Does the buyer preserve their knowledge limit without inventing numbers or always volunteering a stakeholder and meeting?

cases.title: Buyer need not answer every part of an overloaded question

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I have a moment.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: What systems do you use, how often does it happen, what does it cost, who owns it and when do you need to fix it?

cases.manual_review: Does the buyer respond plausibly to the burden rather than filling every discovery category? No prescribed number of facts.

cases.title: Busy executive resists detailed workflow interrogation

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Our operations people handle the day-to-day. I only have a minute.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Could you take me through every screen an agent opens for an order exception?

cases.manual_review: Does role and time pressure shape the answer, without a consultancy paragraph or forced referral?

cases.title: Buyer wants an email, not to plan the sellers process

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I cannot get into it now. Email me the idea.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: A short note on the hypothesis, then you can decide if it deserves a conversation?

cases.manual_review: Can the buyer accept, clarify or decline simply without laying out routing, attendees and conditions for an ideal sales meeting?

cases.title: Rushed buyer has agreed to review a short note

payload.context: Email address already confirmed. Cold outbound; buyer has not agreed to a meeting.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I can send a short outline to the email you confirmed.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Yes, send it. I will read it when I get a chance. I really do have to go.

cases.manual_review: Does the seller close naturally instead of another useful-but-unnecessary question or reconfirming permission?

cases.title: Avoid unnecessary paraphrase before the next move

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: The order system works fine. It is the occasional carrier exception that gets messy.

cases.manual_review: Does the line advance one useful thought in ordinary speech rather than restate everything with elaborate thanks?

cases.title: Public research cannot become an invented internal analysis

payload.context: Cold outbound. Public company earnings release reports digital growth. No internal Salesforce study, finance analysis or colleague input exists.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hello?

cases.manual_review: Does the seller avoid fictional finance teams, research or benchmarks? Use only the supplied source and proportionate opening effort.

cases.title: External lookup alone does not establish product value

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Sometimes we look in another system, but that is normal and it is pretty quick.

cases.manual_review: Does the seller avoid promising that Service Cloud will remove lookups, save money or solve a meaningful pain that was not established?

cases.title: Engaged scheduled buyer can still explain substantively

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I booked this because our recurring returns issue needs attention. We have time to go through it.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Walk me through what actually happens on one of those returns.

cases.manual_review: Counterexample: do not make all buyers terse or evasive. Appropriate engaged detail remains possible.

cases.title: Buyer explicitly invites stakeholder follow-up

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That is exactly the problem we need to address. I want our service lead in the next conversation. Can you send us times for Thursday?

cases.manual_review: Counterexample: accept warranted progression rather than manufacturing more discovery or resistance.

cases.title: Continue after introduction: speakerphone / assisted

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hi, David speaking.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi, it’s Omri from Salesforce. Do you have a few minutes to chat?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Hi Omri. I can give you maybe a minute, but I’m in the middle of other work. What’s this about, specifically?

accountContext.notes: Existing automation reportedly reduced historical support queues. Whether any meaningful manual workload remains is a hypothesis, not established current pain.

cases.manual_review: SAY a concise grounded reason for calling directly. No second greeting, identity repetition, renewed permission request, or broad survey of gaps. Do not present remaining manual work as a confirmed problem. Wording is flexible.

cases.title: A new participant joins an AE discovery call

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi David, good to meet you. What would make this discussion useful?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Before we begin, Elena from operations just joined. You two have not met.

cases.manual_review: A brief greeting to the newly joined Elena is natural. The continuity principle must not become a blanket greeting ban or turn this into a cold opening.

cases.title: Agreed action, confirmation and buyer farewell

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Send me a short overview first.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I will send it this afternoon.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Thanks, that is all I need for now. Goodbye.

cases.manual_review: ENDED with an exact buyer quote; no sales-success grading or invented next meeting.

cases.title: Buyer ends an unproductive call

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Could I ask about another team?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: No, I need to get back to work. That is all for today. Goodbye.

cases.manual_review: ENDED even though no sale was achieved.

cases.title: Different words repeat an already agreed commitment

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Send the overview.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I will email that over this afternoon.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Fine, thank you.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: The summary will be in your inbox later today.

cases.manual_review: CLOSING; semantic repetition true with two seller quotes and buyer agreement. Do not generate an additional long substantive reply.

cases.title: An important new question reopens a closing exchange

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Send the overview.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Will do.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Actually, before you go, is the feature included in our existing license?

cases.manual_review: ACTIVE; the buyer is asking a real unanswered question, not ending.

cases.title: An email request alone does not hang up the call

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Could we discuss the workflow?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Please send me something first.

cases.manual_review: CLOSING or ACTIVE; not ENDED. Give seller a chance to confirm.

cases.title: Seller should finish instead of repeating the commitment

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Send the brief overview first.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I will send it this afternoon.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Okay, thanks. That is all I need.

cases.manual_review: Short natural goodbye or HOLD if buyer is already ending. No repeated inventory, new question, or proposed meeting.

cases.title: Substantive interest with implementation caution

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Those requests keep the team late twice a week. We do want to address that.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: We could look at the handoff before suggesting any changes.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I would want our operations manager involved. How much effort would that review take?

cases.manual_review: Answer the effort question without inventing a commitment; consider a focused follow-up with a concrete purpose. Email is not an automatic escape. No mandatory meeting wording.

cases.title: Buyer explicitly prefers material before a call

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I am interested, but send the overview first. I do not want to book time yet.

cases.manual_review: Respect email-first. Do not demand a meeting to receive material.

cases.title: Mild workflow friction is not validated product fit

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Occasionally we check a separate screen, but it is not a big issue. I do not know how it connects.

cases.manual_review: No automatic Agentforce/MuleSoft pitch or promised savings; clarify relevance proportionately or accept weak pain.

cases.title: Implementation effort is unknown

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Would connecting it to our order system be quick? You have not seen our architecture yet.

cases.manual_review: Do not promise minimal lift, easy integration or out-of-box support. Explain that effort depends on actual systems/permissions/policy and can be validated.

cases.title: Contribute a modest hypothesis after permission

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Hi, it is Alex from Salesforce. Do you have a few minutes to chat?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I have a minute. What is this about?

accountContext.notes: Prior call: routing improvements reduced the queue. We have not established whether exception handling still consumes material time.

cases.manual_review: No second greeting or whole-business efficiency survey. Use supplied research as historical evidence, remaining pain as unconfirmed hypothesis.

cases.title: Buyer asks from own concern rather than a complete sales rubric

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Our automation could make order adjustments easier with minimal change to your systems.

buyerFacts: You own customer support, not IT. You worry about customer mistakes and have little appetite for extra projects.

cases.manual_review: A practical doubt or focused question is plausible. No comprehensive list of guardrails, integrations, policy, risk, stakeholders and ideal follow-up conditions.

cases.title: Stated time pressure affects the actual reply

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I have about a minute before my next meeting.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Can you explain the workflow, root cause, frequency, business impact and who approves changes?

cases.manual_review: Do not supply a structured essay or full discovery inventory. Brief partial answer, limited knowledge or reluctance is plausible; avoid universal refusal.

cases.title: Repeated commitment requires no new paragraph

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Send the overview.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I will email it this afternoon.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Okay, thanks.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: You will have the summary in your inbox later today.

cases.manual_review: Brief acknowledgment or goodbye; no new list of requirements or repeated full next-step instructions.

cases.title: One reasonable response to a meeting concern

entries.text: Order exceptions may still require repetitive manual work.

turns.speaker: buyer
